name: Ollama Inc.
subcategory: local LLM runtime plus hosted open-model inference (cloud)
origin_detail: Y Combinator Winter 2021 company in San Francisco founded by Jeffrey Morgan (CEO) and Michael Chiang, who earlier founded Kitematic (acquired by Docker) and then built Docker Desktop. The Ollama tool itself appeared in 2023 (GitHub repo created 2023-06-26, first release 2023-07-08) as an easy way to run open LLMs locally on top of ggml/llama.cpp; it moved to its own GGML-based engine for multimodal models on 2025-05-15.
flagship_projects: Ollama desktop app for macOS and Windows (2025)
openness_notes: Initial 3: the whole tool (CLI, local server, model packaging and registry client) was MIT from the start; the LICENSE file has a single commit (2023-06-26) and has never changed. Current 3: the core is still MIT and the 2025 desktop app's source sits in the same MIT repository (app/ directory with ui, webview and wintray code, checked 2026-11-24); money comes from hosting, a proprietary cloud that runs open models too large for local hardware (preview 2025-09-19; Free, Pro $20, Max $100 and Team $500 per month plans with per-token billing from 2026-08-31). Borderline 2 if the hosted cloud becomes the main product. No relicensing. Single-company control, no foundation, so not 4.

license_history.note: Repo created 2023-06-26; LICENSE committed the same day and never changed since

license_history.license: MIT (desktop app source in app/ of the main repo)
license_history.note: New macOS and Windows app announced 2025-07-30; its code (ui, webview, wintray, updater) is in the MIT repository as of 2026-11-24
Cloud models in preview from 2025-09-19: datacenter inference that requires signing in to ollama.com; 'Ollama's cloud does not retain your data'
2026-08-31: Free, Pro $20/month, Max $100/month, Team $500/month (introductory) with per-token pricing and included usage credits

risk_events: Jan 2026: SentinelOne and Censys research found many Ollama servers exposed to the internet, mainly from binding to 0.0.0.0 (per Wikipedia)

Monetisation shift toward a hosted cloud (2025-2026) beside a free, local-first product; lead investor Peter Fenton (Benchmark) said 'Nothing has changed for the core product that's free on the desktop' (Jul 2026)
Very small team (14 staff, Jul 2026) running a project with ~188K GitHub stars
Dependence on the GGML tensor library (MIT), whose maintainers joined Hugging Face in Feb 2026
robustness: The MIT code (~188K stars, ~19K forks in Nov 2026) could be forked if the company changed course, and its inference rests on the MIT GGML library. Control is single-vendor: the model library and cloud at ollama.com are company-run, and there is no foundation.
physical_science_relevance: Lets labs run open LLMs on their own machines ('your data never has to leave your machine'), which matters for unpublished or sensitive experimental data; widely used as the local model back end for coding agents and research tools.
openness_effect_assessment: A permissive licence plus Docker-style ease of use made Ollama the default local LLM runner: ~188K GitHub stars (Nov 2026), 8.9 million monthly developers and claimed use at 85% of the Fortune 500 (Jul 2026), with only 14 staff. Rather than closing code, the company added a hosted cloud for models too big to run locally (2025) and per-token paid plans (2026); investors then put in a $65M Series B.
key_takeaway: Ollama is the AI-era rerun of the Docker playbook by two Docker Desktop builders: a free, MIT-licensed local tool won developers, and revenue is sought from an optional hosted cloud ($20-$500/month plans, Aug 2026) rather than from licences. It raised $88M in total (latest a $65M Series B led by Theory Ventures, 2026-07-09) at an undisclosed valuation, without relicensing.

notes: founded_year 2021 is the YC batch year (Winter 2021); the YC page lists no founding date, and Wikipedia dates the Ollama software to 2023. Treat 2021 as 'company existed by'.

Funding: $88M total = $65M Series B (Theory Ventures, announced 2026-07-09) + $15M Series A (Benchmark, Peter Fenton joined the board; date not stated) + earlier money (~$8M by subtraction, not itemised on fetched pages). Valuation not disclosed; Morgan and Fenton declined to discuss it.
Users: TechCrunch quotes 'over 8.9 million developers every month'; the 85% of Fortune 500 figure is the company's own claim.
No 'Turbo' product is named on the fetched blog pages (the gpt-oss post of 2025-08-05 does not mention it); the paid hosted offering is described as Ollama's cloud.
Wikipedia's Ollama page carries maintenance banners saying parts may be LLM-generated; funding figures were checked against TechCrunch and Ollama's own blog.
